items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And so I went out three different times, twice to be with T-Bone and Joe Turner and Eddie Cleanhead.

ctx.x: Congratulations. That’s great. I have a couple of more minutes, and then we’ll wrap up. I did want to mention the T-Bone Walker book. I think it must have been a great deal of work.

Well it was all a pleasure. T-Bone was another personality like Chick. He was a wonderful person, and of course he was a wonderful guitarist, and a wonderful singer. And Stanley and I, Stanley had a friend who sent him records and we first heard him when we were there. And I’ve always loved blues anyways. And so I said to T-Bone in New York, I said, “I’m going to write a book about you.” He never heard of such a thing. And so his wife, who’s still alive and very nice and very sweet, and I said well I’ll come out…
Tim, why don’t you flip that, and then I’ll just wrap this up.
